name: Standard scramble route
descent_text: Reverse the route: down the loose pumice of the south slope to the Echo-Observation saddle, then back along the way trail to Spray Park and the Spray Park Trail to Mowich Lake. Descend south and east only. Dropping west puts you on the crevassed Flett Glacier, which may be impassable late in the season. By August the snow slopes east of the summit can be icy, so carry an ice axe and crampons or microspikes, or circle well above or below them. Wear a helmet, since the rock is crumbly and anything knocked loose falls on those below.
approach: From the Mowich Lake trailhead, take the Spray Park Trail (the Wonderland Trail at first) about 3.5 miles to Spray Park at roughly 5,800 ft. Near 6,200 ft a way trail leaves the main trail, easy to follow for about a mile, and climbs toward the saddle between Echo Rock and Observation Rock near 7,600 ft. Stay on snow where you can to spare the meadows. The north side of Observation is steep and loose, so contour clockwise round the foot of the peak, crossing the east icefield of the Flett Glacier if it is in, to the scree and talus of the south slope, where the climb starts.
